matrix_a_prior_guidance_and_track_record.tooltip_title: Management's official Q3 2026 revenue guidance issued on the Q2 2026 earnings call.
matrix_a_prior_guidance_and_track_record.tooltip_def: Q3 2026 Revenue Guidance: Issued at $61.0B to $64.0B ($62.50B midpoint). Meta has beaten the midpoint of its quarterly revenue guidance in 4 of the last 4 quarters.
matrix_a_prior_guidance_and_track_record.variance_and_sandbag_commentary: CFO Susan Li historically embeds a 150–250 bps conservatism buffer into quarterly revenue guidance; buy-side expects a print near or above the $64.0B top end.

matrix_a_prior_guidance_and_track_record.tooltip_title: Full-Year 2026 capital expenditure guidance corridor issued in Q2 2026.
matrix_a_prior_guidance_and_track_record.tooltip_def: FY2026 CapEx Guidance: Raised in Q2 2026 to $130.0B–$145.0B (including principal payments on finance leases) as Meta scales multi-gigawatt Muse Wonder clusters.
matrix_a_prior_guidance_and_track_record.variance_and_sandbag_commentary: Management has ratcheted the lower bound of CapEx higher every quarter in 2026; expect the corridor to tighten toward $135B–$145B.

matrix_a_prior_guidance_and_track_record.tooltip_title: Full-Year 2026 total operating expense guidance prior to one-time legal accruals.

matrix_b_forward_guidance_bogeys.tooltip_title: The single most important forward number in the Q3 2026 release.
matrix_b_forward_guidance_bogeys.tooltip_def: Q4 2026E Revenue Guide Bogey: Street consensus sits at $71.5B ($70.5B–$72.5B). A guide midpoint above $73.0B+ triggers immediate institutional re-rating.
matrix_b_forward_guidance_bogeys.strategic_rationale: Holiday e-commerce ad budgets and +10% to +14% Advantage+ ad pricing lift must offset macro and FX headwinds to prove AI CapEx is monetizing today.

matrix_b_forward_guidance_bogeys.forward_metric: FY2026 CapEx Corridor & Preliminary FY2027 CapEx Tone
matrix_b_forward_guidance_bogeys.tooltip_title: Capital expenditure trajectory and Free Cash Flow inflection timeline.
matrix_b_forward_guidance_bogeys.tooltip_def: CapEx Bogey: Investors can digest $135B–$145B in FY26 CapEx ONLY if paired with a Q4 revenue guide above $73B and commentary that Reality Labs burn will shrink to help self-fund AI.
matrix_b_forward_guidance_bogeys.strategic_rationale: With Q2 True FCF dipping to -$5,912M ($1,746M Reported FCF minus $7,658M SBC), institutional multiples hinge on whether AI CapEx is self-funded via operating leverage.

matrix_b_forward_guidance_bogeys.forward_metric: Reality Labs FY2026 / FY2027 Operating Loss Trajectory

matrix_b_forward_guidance_bogeys.tooltip_def: Reality Labs Burn Bogey: Buy-side bulls are pressuring CFO Susan Li to cap FY26 RL losses at $18B–$19B and commit to narrowing FY27 RL losses toward ~$15B.
matrix_b_forward_guidance_bogeys.strategic_rationale: Every $3B–$4B reduction in Reality Labs annual burn flows 100% into consolidated GAAP Operating Income and offsets AI server depreciation.

matrix_b_forward_guidance_bogeys.forward_metric: Capital Structure, Buyback Pacing & Share Split Optionality

matrix_b_forward_guidance_bogeys.strategic_rationale: Trading at 18.73x forward P/E ($697.52 spot vs $833.13 average Street target), any shareholder-friendly structural action unlocks immediate multiple expansion.

section_4b_pre_print_debates.debate_title: 1. The $130B–$145B AI CapEx Payback Debate: Muse Wonder ROI vs. Negative True FCF — Framed by JPMorgan & Morgan Stanley
section_4b_pre_print_debates.bull_vs_bear_ framing: Bulls argue that Meta's October 2026 launch of Muse and Muse Wonder (1M-token context, Active Memory, Meta Model API at $4/$20 per M tokens) plus Advantage+ ad ranking (+10% to +14% ad pricing lift) proves immediate, high-margin monetization on GPU clusters. Bears counter that spending ~50% of revenue on CapEx ($30,116M in Q2) pushed Forensic True FCF to -$5,912M and paused aggressive buybacks.
section_4b_pre_print_debates.call_focus_question: What to Listen For on the Call: How does Mark Zuckerberg quantify the direct revenue attribution from Muse / Muse Wonder and Advantage+ in Q3, and will Q4 revenue guidance exceed $73B to prove AI CapEx is immediately accretive?

section_4b_pre_print_debates.debate_title: 2. Operating Margin Resilience Amid Surging AI Server Depreciation & Headcount Discipline — Framed by Goldman Sachs
section_4b_pre_print_debates.bull_vs_bear_framing: Bulls point out that internal deployment of Muse Code and agentic engineering tools is allowing Meta to reduce FTE headcount YoY while scaling annualized revenue past $250B, keeping core operating margins above 35%. Bears warn that 5-year server depreciation from 2025–2026 GPU purchases is ramping >40% YoY, threatening to compress GAAP gross margins below 80%.
section_4b_pre_print_debates.call_focus_question: What to Listen For on the Call: Can CFO Susan Li demonstrate sequential R&D and core G&A leverage via lower FTE headcount, and how should investors separate any one-time legal settlement accruals (e.g., U.S. State AG youth litigation) from normalized operating margins?

section_4b_pre_print_debates.debate_title: 3. Reality Labs Cost Reallocation & Capital Structure Catalyst Watch — Framed by Bank of America & Citi
section_4b_pre_print_debates.bull_vs_bear_framing: Institutional investors are demanding that Meta fund a portion of its AI supercluster buildout by trimming Reality Labs metaverse hardware burn (which lost -$4,839M in Q2 2026). Bulls anticipate an explicit commitment to reduce Reality Labs losses in FY2027 toward ~$15B alongside potential capital structure / stock split catalysts.
section_4b_pre_print_debates.call_focus_question: What to Listen For on the Call: Will management explicitly guide Reality Labs operating losses lower for FY26/FY27 as engineering talent shifts to Meta Superintelligence Labs (MSL) and Ray-Ban Meta AI glasses?
